title: Applying Patient Payments and Choosing the Refund Method on the Insured Plan of Care
content:
**Patient Accounts Manual — Insured Plan of Care, payments and refunds.**

**§1 Taking a payment.** Payments are taken only on a plan that is not closed (intake, active, on hold or discharged).

**§2 Application.** A payment is applied to the patient charge the patient names; when none is named it is applied to the oldest open charge by posting date.

**§3 Credit offset.** Where a payment leaves the plan in credit and the payer program applies credits to other open charges first, the credit is first applied to any other open charge on the same plan.

**§4 Retired clause.** The earlier clause "any remaining credit is refunded within the payer program's credit refund period, in calendar days, after it arose" is **no longer in force**; the refund of credit standing on a plan is governed by the current credit refund basis of the Insured Plan of Care.

**§5 Refund method.** A refund goes back to the original card when it is issued within the payer program's card refund window, in calendar days, of the card payment, and by check otherwise or when the payment was not made by card.

**§6 Ceiling.** A refund never exceeds the payment it returns.

**Evidence.** Whether the plan is closed is read from its status in the system record.

## Applying a payment — hypothetical cases

| Open charges on the plan (hypothetical) | Charge named by the patient | Payment applied to |
|---|---|---|
| Copay posted 2026-02-03; coinsurance posted 2026-03-10 | The coinsurance charge | The coinsurance charge |
| Copay posted 2026-02-03; coinsurance posted 2026-03-10 | None | The copay, the oldest open charge by posting date |

## Refund method — boundary (hypothetical dates, with the 120-calendar-day card refund window scheduled on every payer program)

| Payment | Refund issued | Days after the card payment | Method |
|---|---|---|---|
| Card, 2026-01-10 | 2026-05-10 | 120 | Original card |
| Card, 2026-01-10 | 2026-05-11 | 121 | Check |
| Check or cash | any date | — | Check |

A hypothetical $80.00 card payment can be the subject of a refund of at most $80.00.
